# Antseed

> Antseed is a peer-to-peer network for AI services. You run a local buyer (or a gateway in front of it) that exposes an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API, discovers sellers on a DHT, routes each request to one of them and pays per request in USDC on Base.

If you are an agent, start here: https://antseed.com/skill.md

That skill sets up a gateway, an API key and your tool, step by step.

## Endpoints

- Gateway (recommended): `http://localhost:8379/v1`, or `https://<domain>/v1` on a server. Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, where the key (`antseed_…`) comes from the console or `antseed gateway key create --label <name> --json` (the secret is in `.apiKey`, shown once). Model ids: `deepseek-v4-flash` for automatic routing, or `<peerId>@deepseek-v4-flash` to pin one seller. Console at `/console`; whoever claims it owns the wallets, so give the setup link to your user instead of claiming it yourself.
- Local buyer proxy: `http://localhost:8377/v1`. No API key, listens on `127.0.0.1` only. Anthropic clients use `http://localhost:8377` without `/v1`.
- Both serve `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, and `/v1/models`, plus image, speech and video routes ([list](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/api/#supported-routes)).

Install and start a gateway (it also starts the buyer):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://antseed.com/install.sh | bash
# or
npm install -g @antseed/cli
antseed gateway start
```

## Getting started

- [Skill: join as a buyer](https://antseed.com/skill.md): The agent setup guide. Install, start a gateway, create a key, connect a tool, fund.
- [Introduction](https://antseed.com/docs/): What Antseed is and which way to use it: the Gateway Console, the desktop app or the CLI.
- [Quickstart](https://antseed.com/docs/quickstart/): Run a gateway, claim its console, add funds, create an API key and send your first request.
- [Install](https://antseed.com/docs/install/): Install the gateway, the desktop app or the CLI.

## Gateway Console

- [Gateway and console](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/): What the self-hosted gateway and its console are, and how organizations, workspaces, members and keys fit together.
- [Run a gateway on a server](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/server/): One-command install on a Linux server, published over HTTPS.
- [Move a local gateway to a server](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/migrate/): Move keys, members, workspaces, wallets and usage history.
- [Sign-in and access](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/sign-in/): Claim the console, sign-in methods, inviting members and recovering access.
- [Models and providers](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/models/): Browse models and providers and copy `peer@model` ids.
- [Chat](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/chat/): Chat with any model from the console or the terminal.
- [Funding](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/funding/): Add funds by card or USDC on Base, withdraw, and set the authorized wallet.
- [Budgets and spend limits](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/budgets/): Cap what keys, members and workspaces can spend.
- [Routing policies and presets](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/routing/): Choose which providers may serve requests and save model setups as presets.
- [Calling the API](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/api/): Create API keys and call models from curl, the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs and coding tools.
- [Logs, usage and audit](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/activity/): Spend, tokens, requests and the audit log.
- [Management API](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/management-api/): Script the console with management tokens, and export OpenTelemetry traces.
- [Troubleshooting](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/troubleshooting/): Gateway error codes and how to fix them.
- [Protecting wallet keys](https://antseed.com/docs/gateway/wallet-keys/): Encrypt the gateway's wallet keys with `ANTSEED_PASSPHRASE`.

## Prices and the catalog

Three sources. Say which one you used when you tell a user a price.

1. Your buyer or gateway: `GET /v1/models` lists each model with its sellers and their prices (`.data[].peers[]`, with `peerId`, `displayName`, `inputUsdPerMillion`, `outputUsdPerMillion`). This is what your requests are routed against. Through a gateway, send your key.

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8377/v1/models | jq --arg m deepseek-v4-flash '.data[] | select(.id == $m) | .peers[] | {peerId, displayName, inputUsdPerMillion, outputUsdPerMillion}'
```

2. Cached snapshot, no install or auth: https://network.antseed.com/stats (JSON, from the indexer, a few minutes old; the data behind https://antseed.com/network/). Top-level keys: `peers`, `updatedAt`, `totals`, `indexer`. Provider announcements are at `.peers[].providers[]`, each with `provider`, `services`, `defaultPricing`, `servicePricing[serviceId]` (`inputUsdPerMillion`, `outputUsdPerMillion`, `cachedInputUsdPerMillion`). A service's price is `servicePricing[id] // defaultPricing`, in USD per million tokens. Some peers have an empty `providers` list, so don't read only `.peers[0]`.

```bash
curl -s https://network.antseed.com/stats | jq --arg m deepseek-v4-flash '[.peers[] | .peerId as $id | .providers[] | select(.services | index($m)) | {peerId: $id, price: (.servicePricing[$m] // .defaultPricing)}] | sort_by(.price.inputUsdPerMillion) | .[:5]'
```

3. Live: `antseed network browse --json` (asks peers directly, which takes about a minute, or reads a running buyer's peer list). The shape is different from `/stats`: top-level `source`, `sort`, `filters`, `total`, `peers`, and only the top 20 peers unless you pass `--top <n>`. `.peers[].providers` is a list of provider names, not announcements. Prices are in `.peers[].providerPricing[provider]`: `defaults`, and `services[serviceId]` with the price already resolved. Some peers have no `providerPricing`.

```bash
antseed network browse --json --top 200 | jq --arg m deepseek-v4-flash '[.peers[] | .peerId as $id | (.providerPricing // {}) | to_entries[] | select(.value.services[$m]) | {peerId: $id, provider: .key, price: .value.services[$m]}] | sort_by(.price.inputUsdPerMillion) | .[:5]'
```

## Providers

- [Become a provider](https://antseed.com/docs/provide/): Install the CLI, create a seller identity, register on Base, add services and start serving.
- [Seller configuration](https://antseed.com/docs/provide/config/): Every seller setting in `config.json`: providers, services, pricing, free tier, health checks and payments.
- [Image, video and speech services](https://antseed.com/docs/provide/media/): Per-image, per-video, per-second and per-character pricing.
- [Verified identity](https://antseed.com/docs/provide/verified-identity/): Prove a seller is run by the owner of a domain or GitHub account.
- [TEE seller](https://antseed.com/docs/provide/tee/): Add Intel TDX attestation to a seller.
- [Seller payments](https://antseed.com/docs/provide/payments/): How a seller gets paid in USDC on Base, gas, and claiming rewards.
- [ANTS staking](https://antseed.com/docs/provide/staking/): Stake ANTS into seller pools and claim rewards.
- [Monitoring](https://antseed.com/docs/provide/monitoring/): The seller dashboard, trust score, alerts and Prometheus health metrics.
- [Metrics](https://antseed.com/docs/provide/metrics/): Export requests, tokens, channels and USDC flow to Prometheus.
- [Provider plugin API](https://antseed.com/docs/provider-api/): Build a provider plugin for your own upstream, agent or model.
- [Router plugin API](https://antseed.com/docs/router-api/): How the buyer chooses a seller, and how to write your own routing policy.

Antseed is for value-added services (TEEs, agents, fine-tunes, managed products), not resale of API keys or subscription access.

## Security and verification

- [Verify a seller's TEE](https://antseed.com/docs/verify-tee/): Check that a seller runs in a genuine Intel TDX enclave, and require it.
- [Model verification](https://antseed.com/docs/verify/overview/): How Antseed checks that sellers serve the models they advertise.
- [Model verification for buyers](https://antseed.com/docs/verify/buyers/): How verification affects routing, and how to check a seller yourself.
- [Model verification for providers](https://antseed.com/docs/verify/providers/): How your services are audited and what results mean.
- [Become a verifier](https://antseed.com/docs/verify/): Set up a verifier and run a KBF audit.
- [How audits run](https://antseed.com/docs/verify/audits/): Which models and sellers are audited and how verdicts go on-chain.

## Protocol

- [Protocol overview](https://antseed.com/docs/overview/): The layers, from DHT discovery to USDC settlement and reputation.
- [Peer discovery](https://antseed.com/docs/discovery/): How sellers announce on the DHT and buyers validate signed metadata.
- [Transport](https://antseed.com/docs/transport/): Handshake, transport modes, framing and message types.
- [Payments and metering](https://antseed.com/docs/payments/): USDC payment channels on Base, metering, free usage and fees.
- [Model routing](https://antseed.com/docs/model-routing/): Routing services: seller services that rank where a buyer should send a request.
- [Reputation](https://antseed.com/docs/reputation/): How buyers compute a 0-100 trust score for each seller.
- [Security](https://antseed.com/docs/security/): Identity, key storage, signing roles and risk limits.
- [Recognized usage](https://antseed.com/docs/recognized-usage/): How paid usage turns into ANTS rewards.
- [Reward policies](https://antseed.com/docs/reward-policies/): Points policies, including the model-verification bonus and penalty.
- [Model verification (protocol)](https://antseed.com/docs/model-verification/): The KBF audit and its on-chain results.
